full_texts.title: Portugal municipality working on implementing tourist tax - The Portugal News
full_texts.text:
“The City Council has approved the proposed tourist tax regulations, to take effect in January,” José Rodrigues Paredes, mayor of the municipality in the Vila Real district, told the Lusa news agency.
Alijó could be the first municipality within the Douro Intermunicipal Community (CIM) to move forward with creating a tourist tax, though the matter has long been discussed in the region.
The municipal executive has now approved the regulations, which will undergo a 30-day public consultation period before the Alijó Municipal Assembly discusses and votes on them; the tax is expected to take effect on 1 January 2027.
“This tourist tax has a dual structure: an overnight stay fee of two euros and an arrival fee of two euros for those entering the municipality of Alijó by river,” explained José Rodrigues Paredes.
The mayor justified the decision by citing strain on infrastructure and visitors’ increasingly high expectations, which compel the municipality to invest more and require additional resources.
He cited Pinhão, a town along the Douro River where many visitors arrive by tourist boat.
“The pressure on infrastructure is such that it becomes practically impossible to get around Pinhão during the summer,” he noted.
Many of these river tourists quickly move on to other municipalities, but, according to José Rodrigues Paredes, Alijó welcomes them, collects their municipal solid waste, supplies water to the vessels (in significant volumes), and provides electricity.
“The municipality has to bear all these costs; therefore, it must find new revenue sources to continue welcoming tourists and providing them with the highest quality service,” he emphasised.
He further noted that 50% of the revenue from the tourist tax will go to the farmers, the “creators of the landscape”, who tend the vineyards, terraces, and schist walls that were granted UNESCO status 25 years ago.
“All of this exists only because of the Douro landscape, but someone creates that landscape, someone maintains it, and someone preserves it... At the same time, we are exploring ways to eventually transfer a portion of this tax to those who actually care for our Douro landscape,” he stressed.
According to the mayor, the arrival fee for river travel will apply only to large-capacity vessels (hotel boats). The Administration of the Ports of Douro, Leixões, and Viana do Castelo (APDL), the entity that manages the Douro waterway, will collect it.
“It is the APDL that licenses all river activity and, therefore, knows exactly how many tourists each vessel carries. We have an understanding on this, and the APDL will be the one to collect the fee and subsequently transfer it to the municipality of Alijó,” he noted.
The Douro region has discussed implementing a fee, whether a tourist tax or a sustainability levy, to support winegrowers.
“It is true that there is no consensus; not all municipalities align with the same idea. Some advocate for a broad-based fee, potentially even managed by an external entity—something I do not agree with at all,” he stated.
José Rodrigues Paredes added that he is not alone in this decision and that neighbouring municipalities also intend to move forward with creating such a fee.
“We must move forward because the Douro region needs to provide a quality experience for those who wish to enjoy its beauty, its products, and the friendliness of its people; however, those who live here must also have the means and resources to invest and keep this region alive,” he maintained.

full_texts.title: European Defence Agency to test drones and loitering munitions in Portugal with more than 200 military and industry participants - Defence Industry Europe
full_texts.text:
The programme is designed to give armed forces evidence of what the technologies can do outside controlled demonstrations. Unmanned systems, loitering munitions and electronic communications will be assessed for their performance, interoperability and potential operational use.
EU OPEX is being held within ARTEX 26, the Portuguese Army’s annual experimentation campaign. The event also brings in BraveTech EU, an EU-Ukraine defence innovation initiative, and the Sentinel Strike contest, whose five loitering munition finalists are competing for €1.8 million in prizes.
Testing will start with individual systems and missions in a single domain before moving to more complex scenarios. The later stages are intended to show how different technologies work together across land and air operations.
The planned missions include drones sending reconnaissance information to commanders from a hostile environment. Aerial and ground systems will work together to move supplies to frontline troops, while loitering munitions will be tasked with engaging multiple targets at night.
Cross-domain field tests are scheduled for 7 and 8 October. A further event on 14 October will bring political leaders, military representatives and defence stakeholders to observe demonstrations and examine the technologies tested during the campaign.

full_texts.title: SIFC advances Pakistan-Portugal investment cooperation - The Nation (Pakistan )
full_texts.text:
The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and Ambassador of Portugal Paulo Domingues on Saturday discussed ways to enhance bilateral economic, trade and investment cooperation, with particular focus on textiles, agriculture, information technology, pharmaceuticals and Special Economic Zones (SEZs).
The SIFC hosted the Ambassador of Portugal for a wide-ranging discussion focused on strengthening economic, trade and investment cooperation between Pakistan and Portugal, according to a press release issued by SIFC.
The engagement provided an opportunity to explore areas of mutual interest and identify promising avenues for greater collaboration between the business communities of both countries.
Discussions covered investment opportunities in textiles, agriculture, information and communication technology, pharmaceuticals and Special Economic Zones (SEZs), highlighting the potential for enhanced commercial engagement and investment partnerships.
SIFC briefed the Ambassador on Pakistan’s investment potential across priority sectors and its investor-centric facilitation framework aimed at providing coordinated support to domestic and international investors.
As a whole-of-government platform, SIFC works to facilitate engagement between investors and relevant federal, provincial and sectoral stakeholders, helping streamline investment processes and support the development of viable business opportunities.
The meeting also highlighted opportunities emerging from Pakistan’s growing connectivity with international businesses and institutions.
In this context, SIFC acknowledged the launch of FC Porto’s Dragon Force Academy in Sialkot, established in partnership with Forward Sports. The initiative brings the renowned Portuguese football club’s youth development programme to Pakistan and represents an additional avenue for strengthening institutional and commercial linkages between the two countries.
The engagement underscored the scope for expanding Pakistan-Portugal cooperation through investment, business partnerships and sector-specific opportunities.
SIFC emphasized the importance of continued engagement with international partners to identify commercially viable projects and create stronger linkages between Pakistani and Portuguese investors and businesses.
SIFC reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating international investors through coordinated government support, providing greater clarity on investment opportunities and promoting an enabling environment for mutually beneficial partnerships.
